style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The shortest lament in the Psalter, and the one that gives the church its permission to ask 'how long?' -- four times in two verses. David is being forgotten, God's face is hidden, his own planning goes in circles, sorrow sits in his heart all day, and the enemy is on top. The prayer in the middle is small and exact: look at me, answer me, put light back in my eyes before I sleep the sleep of death and my enemy gets to say 'I beat him.' Then, with nothing in the situation changed, the psalm turns on one word: but. But I -- I have put my trust in Your covenant love; my heart will exult in Your salvation; I will sing to the LORD, because He has dealt generously with me. Six verses that travel from 'forever?' to song -- the shape of every honest prayer that has ever worked its way from complaint to trust. Calvin read the 'how longs' as the language of faith, not its failure.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of David. How long, O LORD -- will You keep forgetting me forever? How long will You keep Your face hidden from me?
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. How long will You forget [shakach] me, O LORD [YHWH]? for ever [netsach]? how long will You hide [satar] Your face [panim] from me?
1.notes: ad-anah, 'how long' -- four times in two verses, the lament's refrain. tishkacheni netsach (H7911, H5331): forget me FOREVER? -- the same pair Psalm 9:18 uses to promise that the needy shall not always (netsach) be forgotten (shakach), now turned into a fear that the promise has lapsed. tastir et-panekha (H5641, H6440): the hidden face, the reversal of Aaron's blessing.

2.text: How long must I keep laying plans in my soul, with sorrow in my heart all day long? How long will my enemy stand tall over me?
2.amp: How long shall I take [shith -- set, lay out] counsel [etsah -- plans] in my soul [nephesh], having sorrow [yagon] in my heart [lebab] daily [yomam -- by day]? how long shall mine enemy [oyeb] be exalted [rum] over me?
2.notes: ashit etsot be-naphshi (H7896, H6098, H5315): laying plan after plan inside himself -- the restless, daylong scheming that goes nowhere -- with yagon bi-lebabi yomam (H3015, H3824, H3119), sorrow in the heart all day. And the fourth 'how long': yarum oyevi alai (H7311, H341), the enemy standing tall over him.

3.text: Look at me and answer me, O LORD my God! Put light back in my eyes, or I will sleep the sleep of death --
3.amp: Consider [nabat -- look at] and hear [anah -- answer] me, O LORD [YHWH] my God [Elohim]: lighten [or] mine eyes [ayin], lest I sleep [yashen] the sleep of death [mavet];
3.notes: Three imperatives after four questions: habbitah, aneni (H5027, H6030) -- look, answer -- and hairah enai (H215, H5869), light my eyes: in Hebrew the eyes go dim in sickness and grief and 'lighten' when life returns (cf. 1 Samuel 14:27). pen-ishan ha-mavet (H3462, H4194): the sleep of death, the eye's final dimming.

4.text: or my enemy will say, 'I have beaten him,' and my adversaries will exult when I am toppled.
4.amp: Lest mine enemy [oyeb] say [amar], I have prevailed [yakol] against him; and those that trouble [tsar] me rejoice [gil] when I am moved [mot -- shaken, toppled].
4.notes: The stake is not only David's life but God's reputation: pen-yomar oyevi yekholtiv (H559, H341, H3201) -- 'I beat him' -- and tsarai yagilu ki emmot (H6862, H1523, H4131): the adversaries exulting at his toppling. The gil of the wrong crowd is what verse 5 will reclaim.

5.text: But I -- in Your covenant love I have put my trust; my heart will exult in Your salvation.
5.amp: But I have trusted [batach] in Your mercy [chesed -- covenant love]; my heart [leb] shall rejoice [gil -- exult] in Your salvation [yeshuah].
5.notes: va-ani -- but I: the psalm turns on the pronoun, with nothing in the situation changed. be-chasdekha batachti (H2617, H982): the trust is past tense, already placed; yagel libbi bi-yeshuatekha (H1523, H3820, H3444): the exulting is future -- and it is the enemies' gil (v. 4) taken back for the right heart.

6.text: I will sing to the LORD, because He has dealt generously with me.
6.amp: I will sing [shir] unto the LORD [YHWH], because He has dealt bountifully [gamal -- dealt fully, ripened] with me.
6.notes: ashirah la-YHWH (H7891): six verses from 'forever?' to song. ki gamal alai (H1580): gamal is the full-dealing verb -- to ripen, to wean, to pay out in full -- and the tense is perfect: David sings of a completed bounty while the enemy is still, as far as we know, exalted. Faith reports the verdict before the trial ends.
